chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Sa'id who said: He narrated to me Musa ibn Uqayl from al-A'la ibn Umayr, the freedman of the family of Sam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
What was the size of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? He said: 'Three thousand and six hundred cubits, fractional.'

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Mosque of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What were the exact dimensions of the Prophet's mosque according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the reverence for the Prophet’s Mosque by specifying its exact area as 3,600 cubits, a measurement often interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the total enclosed space including courtyards and prayer halls. The precise quantification underscores the theological importance of physical spaces dedicated to worship in Islamic tradition, serving as a benchmark for the sanctity of mosques. This detail is frequently cited in discussions regarding the architectural and spiritual significance of the Masjid al-Nabawi in Shia jurisprudence and history.
